newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks open stronger on Wall Street gains.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks open stronger on Wall Street gains.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index soared 155 points, or 1.13 percent, to 13,895 at the open on Friday, with sentiment boosted by a recovery on Wall Street and overnight gains by Hong Kong stocks in London, brokers said.
The Dow industrials rose 50.97 points to 7,136.62 on Thursday and the Hang Seng London Reference Index jumped 189.78 points to 13,930.08.
"The early rally is mainly led by HSBC Holdings, which opened sharply higher," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J & A Securities.
HSBC Holdings surged HK$5.00 to HK$215.00 after hitting a record high of HK$218.00.
The trading suspensions of Hongkong Telecom and CITIC Pacific, both at the request of the companies, capped the Hang Seng Index's rise, brokers said.

With expectations mounting that Hongkong Telecom could link up with a Chinese partner, brokers said investors were speculating CITIC Pacific could sell part or all of its eight percent stake in Hongkong Telecom to China United Telecommunications Corp.
The blue-chip index backed down slightly from its early high of 13,974.45 to trade 154 points higher at 13,894.
"There is some pressure near the 14,000 level but selling is not heavy," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
He expected CITIC Pacific and Hongkong Telecom to bring the index to new highs after they resume trading. "CITIC should earn a big profit from the deal," he said.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong added HK$0.75 to HK$74.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$1.00 to HK$91.75.
H-shares were hit by profit-taking, with the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index down nine points, or 0.79 percent, at 1,135.
May Hang Seng Index futures added 200 points to 13,885 at mid-morning. -- Alison Leung (852) 2843 6369
